commitResults.messageTitle: Store parent-student links in the address book
commitResults.messageBody:
Tutors cannot record which parent belongs to which student, so they
must remember the relationship themselves when contacting families.

Let's store parent-student links beside the contacts in AddressBook
and persist them as a "links" list in the data file.

Each side of a link is identified by its normalized name and phone,
matching the duplicate-contact rules, so no new ID field is needed
and the saved file stays easy to edit by hand. Deleting a contact
removes its links, and editing a linked name or phone rewrites them,
so links never point to missing contacts. Files without "links"
still load, keeping existing data files compatible.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add link command and show linked contacts in view
commitResults.messageBody:

them or to see them, so the stored links are not yet useful.

Let's add `link PARENT_INDEX STUDENT_INDEX`, using displayed-list
indices like view and delete, and list linked students or parents in
the expanded contact card.

The command rejects wrong roles, self-links, and duplicate links
without changing data. It expands the parent after linking so the
user sees the result immediately. Delete now reports how many links
it removed, so the cascade is never silent. The sample data includes
two links so new users can see the feature on first launch.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable assertions when running the app with Gradle
commitResults.messageBody:

add `-ea` to the IntelliJ run configuration.

Tests already run with assertions enabled under Gradle, so only the
run task and IDE configuration need changing. The released JAR is
unaffected, so end users never see assertion failures.

commitResults.messageBody:

identity-based hash codes. Equal instances can therefore be missed or
stored twice in hash-based collections.

hashing to its predicate. Add regression tests that verify equal hashes,
lookup, and duplicate rejection for independently constructed instances.
